A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, Lost in Translation, Found in Context. Their main text, figures, tables, mathematical descriptions, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V1 reports original BOBSL and How2Sign experiments, PHOENIX14T baseline reproductions, ablations, and a human evaluation involving five annotators and 70 translations.

after.justification: V2 retains these empirical results and adds BOBSL sensitivity experiments, additional comparison configurations, and evaluation of the proposed model on PHOENIX14T.

M1.justification: The proposed Video-Swin/mapping-network/Llama3 framework, cue construction, LoRA training, loss, augmentations, and autoregressive inference remain unchanged. The added experiments vary configurations or apply the existing framework to PHOENIX14T rather than introduce a new translation procedure.

E1.justification: BOBSL, How2Sign, and PHOENIX14T were already used in v1, including original baseline reproductions in Appendix B.5. V2 adds proposed-model results on PHOENIX14T and parameter sweeps within BOBSL, without introducing different represented data or task requirements.

E2.justification: Named external baselines are retained. Within Table 3, v2 adds video-only, reduced-cue, and matched-input oracle versions of the proposed model as comparators, while removing the Vid+PrevGT+PG+BG oracle configuration. SignLLM is discussed but not evaluated as a baseline.

E3.justification: Section 4.2 changes Sincan's reported oracle context from three previous ground-truth sentences to one, without establishing that experiments were rerun. New experiments vary history length and background-caption intervals from one to three sentences/seconds during training and inference. Existing principal splits, metrics, and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 substantially extends diagnostic coverage with history-length and background-sampling sensitivity studies in Appendices B.4–B.5, matched-input oracle and video-only controls in Table 3, and a PHOENIX14T pseudo-gloss ablation in Table A.11. These examine previously untested design choices and better separate model advantages from additional input information.

E5.justification: The five-annotator, 70-translation evaluation and its averaging and correlation analyses are retained. Neither version supplies repeated-training-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the translation results.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial results: PHOENIX14T video-only versus video-plus-pseudo-gloss BLEU-4 scores of 20.58 versus 23.80, both sensitivity sweeps, and additional BOBSL controls. Table 3 removes the 41.6 BLEURT Vid+PrevGT+PG+BG result and adds 40.5 for Vid+PrevGT; these are different settings, not a performance decline. Retained headline BOBSL and How2Sign scores are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical descriptions, feature notation, loss, and evaluation-metric definitions remain unchanged. Neither version introduces theoretical propositions, formal guarantees, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same contributions: contextual translation, cue analysis, LLM-based evaluation, BOBSL improvements, and How2Sign generalisation. The conclusion preserves the central claim that context improves translation; new experiments provide supporting evidence.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly identifies error propagation from previous predicted sentences, explains efficiency tradeoffs behind the context and sampling defaults, and qualifies PHOENIX14T as lacking discourse/background context and having restricted vocabulary. Existing qualitative failure cases and limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix B.8 specifies that the PHOENIX14T Video-Swin features use training pseudo-glosses obtained from SlowFastSign. The acknowledgments newly identify the source of Sincan's test outputs and assistance with Sign2GPT implementation. Existing hardware, hyperparameters, prompts, and resource-access statements are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds a brief discussion of SignLLM and citations for that work, its LLaMA backbone, and SlowFastSign. The broader positioning relative to Sincan, GFSLT, and Sign2GPT remains unchanged.

P1.justification: There are targeted revisions to the comparison discussion and conclusion, a short homonym explanation, additional appendix subsections, and affiliation and acknowledgment edits. The overall narrative and section organisation remain stable.

P2.justification: Table 3 is expanded and grouped into VIDEO ONLY, EXTRA CUES, and ORACLE blocks. Three appendix tables are added, with existing tables relocated or renumbered. The figures, plots, and qualitative illustrations are retained, with limited layout adjustments.

improvement.justification: Table 3's matched-input controls make the comparisons more informative, while the new sensitivity studies support the existing design choices. PHOENIX14T results and explicit error-propagation limitations strengthen the evidence and clarify applicability. These are useful incremental improvements to a paper whose central method and principal findings were already supported in v1.
